# Contributing to Bridlewise

Bridlewise is built in the open: the harness, its tests, its guards and its
decision records live in [LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing). People and agents
contribute through the same door: the same pull request flow, the same checks
and the same independent review.

> [!WARNING]
> Bridlewise is an experimental developer preview. Do not use it on sensitive,
> proprietary, regulated or production codebases; run it against disposable
> copies. Never include real credentials, private source, personal data or local
> database contents in an issue, fixture, screenshot or pull request.

## Ways to help

- **Report a problem** through an issue form (listed below); each asks only what
  a triager needs.
- **Ask, propose or show** in [Discussions](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing/discussions) (see
  [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) for the categories).
- **Pick up work** labelled [`good first issue`](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing/labels/good%20first%20issue)
  or [`help wanted`](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing/labels/help%20wanted).
- **Review** an open pull request: say what you checked and what you could not.
- **See what is coming:** the [planned community features](SUPPORT.md#planned),
  each linked to its tracking issue.

The issue forms:

- [Bug report](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing/issues/new?template=bug.yml): Report a reproducible problem in the developer preview.
- [Flake report](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing/issues/new?template=flake.yml): A test that passed and failed on the same tree. Name the test file and the test.
- [Docs fix](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing/issues/new?template=docs.yml): A page that is wrong, stale, unclear or missing.

## Your first contribution

The whole path, end to end; each step links the section that has the detail.

1. **Pick something small.** An issue labelled
   [`good first issue`](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing/labels/good%20first%20issue), or a
   docs page you found wrong. Say in the issue that you are taking it, so two
   people do not do the same work.
2. **Fork and clone** the repository, then follow [Setup](#setup).
3. **Make one change on a branch,** with a test when it changes behavior
   ([Test conventions](#test-conventions)), and run the local gate:
   `cd engine && node src/cli.ts harness check`.
4. **Commit with a sign-off:** `git commit -s` (the
   [commit style](#commit-and-pull-request-style) has the details).
5. **Open a pull request against `main`** and fill in its template.
6. **Wait for the first CI run.** A first-time contributor's first run waits
   for a maintainer's one-time approval; after that, CI runs on every push.
7. **Answer the review.** Someone other than you verifies the change and says
   what they checked; push fixes to the same branch.
8. **It lands** once the required checks and the review are green
   ([How your pull request lands](#how-your-pull-request-lands)).

Stuck at any step? Ask in [Discussions](https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing/discussions) or on
the issue.

## Setup

Requirements: Linux, Node `>=24.18.0 <25.0.0`, npm, Git, `gcc-14` (the
guardian's pinned compiler; on Debian or Ubuntu install it with
`sudo apt-get install -y gcc-14`), and optionally Playwright Chromium for
the browser tests.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/LLM-4-People/bridlewise-testing.git
cd bridlewise-testing
npm ci
npm --prefix engine ci
npm run bootstrap:hooks
chmod 600 engine/bridlewise.config.json
make -C engine/guardian all
npm --prefix engine run build:bundle
```

Before you open a pull request, run the local gate:

```bash
cd engine && node src/cli.ts harness check
```

[docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns the suites, their prerequisites and what
CI runs.

## What makes a good change

The [mandatory engineering rules](docs/process/AGENTS.md#mandatory-engineering-rules)
and the [evidence bar](docs/process/AGENTS.md#evidence) bind every change; the
[agent process](docs/process/AGENTS.md#what-we-will-not-accept) owns what the
project will not accept. This page keeps the contribution mechanics around them.

- Validate at trust boundaries: paths, schema fields, finite numbers, uniqueness and cross-field invariants.
- Make multi-step state changes atomic, and give background work ownership, cancellation, timeout and shutdown.
- Update the docs when a command, route, config key or user-visible behavior changes.
- Generated files (hashes, pins, inventories, these community files) come from
  `cd engine && node src/cli.ts harness sync`, never from a hand edit.

## Test conventions

Where a test goes, which runner it uses and how it stays deterministic are
owned by [Adding a test](docs/testing.md#adding-a-test). Whether a reproduced
bug's test must fail before the fix is part of the [evidence
bar](docs/process/AGENTS.md#evidence).

## Commit and pull request style

- **Stage with `npm run stage -- <new path>…`** (`harness stage`): it stages
  every tracked file you changed plus each new file you name, by its literal
  path, and nothing unnamed. It refuses a path that does not exist, a folder,
  an ignored file (naming the rule), a conflicted file still holding its
  markers, and a change that would drop a staged blob existing nowhere else.
  Never `git add -A`, `git add .` or `git commit -a`, even with a path.
- **Sign off every commit** with the [Developer Certificate of
  Origin](https://developercertificate.org/): `git commit -s` adds
  `Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.com>`, matching the commit's author. To
  fix a pull request that lacks it, run `git rebase --signoff main` and push
  again. Commits made in GitHub's web editor are signed off by GitHub.
- **Sign your commits** (SSH signing is three lines):
  `git config gpg.format ssh`,
  `git config user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`,
  `git config commit.gpgsign true`, then add the key to GitHub as a signing key.
- Conventional prefixes: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`.
- One logical change per pull request. Describe what changed, how it was
  verified and what could not be verified.
- Link the relevant decision record or design document when the change is
  architectural.
- By submitting a contribution, you agree that it is licensed under AGPL-3.0-only.

## How your pull request lands

1. Fork the repository and open a pull request against `main`. `main` takes
   pull requests only: nobody pushes to it directly, maintainers included.
2. CI runs on the `pull_request` event with a read-only token and no secrets,
   for every author alike. A first-time contributor's first run waits for a
   maintainer's one-time approval; after that, CI runs on every push.
3. Someone other than the author verifies the change before it lands (see
   [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md) for whose approval counts).
4. It lands as a merge commit once the required checks and the review are
   green; the issues it resolves close when it lands.

## Talking to the bots

On an issue or a pull request, a comment whose first line is a command goes to
the harness. The publisher App answers each command comment once, and a triage command (`/accept`, `/decline`, `/duplicate`) opens a pull request adding the issue's record.

| Command | Where | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/help` | issue, pull request | Contributor and above | list the commands and who may use them |
| `/status [<record-id> or #<n>]` | issue, pull request | Contributor and above | the record's state, lane, milestone, severity and blockers, read from the harness's records (this issue's when none is named) |
| `/accept <P0-P3> <milestone> [<parent-id>]` | issue | Triager and above | adopt this intake issue: the harness opens a pull request adding its record |
| `/decline <reason>` | issue | Triager and above | record the intake as not planned, with the reason, through a pull request |
| `/duplicate #<n>` | issue | Triager and above | record the intake as a duplicate of #n, through a pull request |
| `/explain` | pull request | Contributor and above | the door's explanation of this pull request's verdict: the failing gate, its evidence and its owning record |

- The command starts the comment: a quoted, indented or mid-text command is
  never run, so quoting someone does not repeat what they typed.
- Who may run a command comes from your permission on the repository, through
  the [role table](GOVERNANCE.md#roles), never from how GitHub labels you.
- A bot never changes an issue's state itself. A triage command adds a record
  through a pull request, reviewed and landed like any other.
- Type `/help` on any issue or pull request for this table as the bot knows it.

## AI-assisted contributions

AI-assisted work is welcome. You remain responsible for the result. Disclose
material assistance, verify every claim, and do not paste unreviewed generated
code into safety, privacy, auth or persistence paths. The project's own agents
land their work through the same pull requests, checks and review.

## Review

Review applies the [evidence bar](docs/process/AGENTS.md#evidence) through the
[reviewer role](docs/process/ROLES.md#reviewer). A green CI run is necessary but
not sufficient: changes that make the preview look more complete than it is may
be declined.

## Code of conduct

Participation is covered by [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
